statement: The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone.
notes: Literal absolute Loc (3) is not the adopted relative axiom.

statement: Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
notes: No two-out-of-three needed for composition and base-change closure; retract premise explicit.

statement: The coarse, universal, and local relative classes. Suppose $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal L$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition and pullback. For an arrow $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal M/S$, put \[ u\in W_S^{\mathcal L}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(X\times_S T\longrightarrow Y\times_S T\bigr)\in W \quad\hbox{for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L. \] Let $W_S^u$ be the same class with all $T\to S$ allowed. Then \[ W_S^u\subseteq W_S^{\mathcal L}\subseteq W_S. \] All three classes contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Their retract closure follows if $W$ has it. These are precisely the relative classes in XII ms.~210 and 220. They must not be confused with the class of universal $W$-equivalences in $\mathcal M$, where the base is the codomain of the arrow being tested.
notes: Full faithfulness on coefficients need not satisfy two-out-of-three.

statement: What raw reindexing and postcomposition actually preserve. Under the hypotheses of A.3, a map $f:S'\to S$ in $\mathcal L$ induces \[ f^*:(\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L}). \] For every $f:S'\to S$, without assuming $f\in\mathcal L$, postcomposition induces \[ f_\#:(\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L}). \] If $f^*$ also preserves the displayed classes, the ordinary adjunction $f_\#\dashv f^*$ descends to their localizations. For arbitrary $f$, this calculation alone constructs the descended postcomposition functor; it does not construct its right adjoint.
notes: Raw pullback is proved homotopical only for the stated class; postcomposition works for every map.

statement: The universal saturation of the local test class. Under A.3, define $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ by the following condition on $f:S'\to S$: for every $T\to S$, pullback along $f_T:T\times_S S'\to T$ sends $W_T^{\mathcal L}$ into $W_{T\times_S S'}^{\mathcal L}$. Then $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ contains $\mathcal L$, contains isomorphisms, and is closed under composition and pullback. Moreover \[ W_S^{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=W_S^{\mathcal L} \quad\hbox{for every }S,\qquad \widehat{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=\widehat{\mathcal L}. \] It is the largest composition- and pullback-closed class containing isomorphisms that defines this same family of fine relative classes. This is the corrected, second definition at XII ms.~222; the first definition on that page omits the universal quantifier over $T\to S$.
notes: The preliminary base-change universal quantifier is indispensable.

statement: The corrected transporter Galois connection. Let $W$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition in a category $\mathcal M$ with pullbacks. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections. Their extreme pairs are \[ (W^u,\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M),\qquad (W,\operatorname{Fib}_W), \] where $W^u$ means universal equivalences with respect to the codomain of each arrow.
notes: Right-hand domain requires pullback closure, not composition closure.

statement: The exact composition criterion, II Proposition 6.1. For a closed pair $A=K_W(L)$, $L=T_W(A)$ of A.6, the following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is composition-closed; pullback along every member of $L$ preserves $A$; and $L=\operatorname{Stab}(A)$, where $\operatorname{Stab}(A)=T_A(A)$. Every stabilizer is composition- and pullback-closed. In particular, a transporter into the larger class $W$ is not generally a stabilizer.
notes: Correct composition criterion for a closed transporter pair.

statement: Transporters need not compose under the hypotheses of II section 6. The claim in the first version of II~(6.2)--(6.5) that $T_W(A)$ automatically belongs to a right-hand domain requiring composition closure is false. A counterexample is the chain category $0<1<2<3$, with $W$ consisting of the identities and $0\to2,0\to3$, and $A$ consisting of the identities and $0\to3$. Here \[ T_W(A)=\operatorname{Mor}([3])\setminus\{1\to3\},\qquad K_WT_W(A)=A. \] Consequently $1\to2$ and $2\to3$ lie in the transporter while their composite does not.
notes: W is composition-closed but not two-out-of-three, exactly as permitted in II section 6.

statement: The meaning of smooth and proper in the manuscript. For a fundamental localizer on $\mathrm{Cat}$, let $\operatorname{As}_W$ consist of $u:A\to B$ for which $A/b\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$, and let $\operatorname{Coas}_W$ consist of $u$ for which $b\backslash A\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$. The definitions used at II ms.~66 and explicitly reaffirmed at ms.~89 are \[ \operatorname{Liss}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{As}_W), \qquad \operatorname{Prop}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{Coas}_W). \] The two mixed transporters contain both the corresponding stabilizer and $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Neither is the definition of smoothness or properness. The proposed inclusion $\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$ at XII ms.~225--226 is explicitly qualified by ``peut-\^etre'' and is an extra proposed axiom, not a consequence asserted to have been proved there.
notes: Smooth/proper are asphericity stabilizers, not the mixed transporters into W.

statement: The three fibre axioms, with their quantifiers. For every $S\in\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal F_S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal M/S$ on the intrinsic fibrations. The three assertions at XII ms.~215--218 are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{(a)}&\quad J_S:\mathcal F_S[(W_S^u)^{-1}] \longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]\text{ is an equivalence};\\ \mathrm{(b)}&\quad W_S^u=W_S\text{ on }\mathcal F_S;\\ \mathrm{(c)}&\quad\mathcal F_S[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow \mathcal H[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}] \text{ are equivalences} \end{aligned} \] for every full $\mathcal F_S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$. Axiom (a) implies equality of the strong saturations of $W_S^u$ and $W_S$ on $\mathcal F_S$. It does not by that argument imply equality of the original classes. Axioms (b) and (c) imply (a).
notes: Axiom a gives equality of strong saturations; b is equality of the original restricted classes.

statement: Enough intrinsic fibrations implies the exact fibrewise invariance. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has pullbacks, $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three, and every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Then axiom (b) of A.10 holds, and \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W\cap W=W^u. \] No terminal object, accessibility, functorial factorization, or strong saturation is required for these conclusions.
notes: No chosen functorial factorization or terminal object needed.

statement: A functorial replacement proves every intermediate-subcategory comparison. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category with a class $W$ containing isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three, let $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A$ be full, and suppose there is $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ with a natural transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal A}\to iR$ whose components are in $W$. For every full $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal A$, both inclusions induce equivalences \[ \mathcal F[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal H[W^{-1}] \longrightarrow\mathcal A[W^{-1}]. \] In particular, such slice replacements into $\operatorname{Fib}_W S$, together with enough intrinsic fibrations, verify XII (a), (b), and (c).
notes: Sufficient extra replacement hypothesis, not proof from a and b alone.

statement: The implication asked in audit row XIIc B062. The axioms (a) and (b) of A.10, even imposed at every base, do not imply (c). There is a counterexample with six objects, all finite limits and colimits, and strongly saturated $W$. It also refutes the analogous assertion for enhanced localizations.
notes: Six-object finite lattice refutes a+b implies c at every-base scope; W strongly saturated; enhanced version also fails.

statement: The two fine axiom systems in XII ms.225--227. Suppose classes $L,P\subseteq\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M$ contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition and pullback. Define $W_S^g=W_S^L$ and $W_S^d=W_S^P$. The clause called (a) on ms.~226, asserting preservation of $W^g$ by $L$-base change and of $W^d$ by $P$-base change, follows formally from the closure hypotheses. The clause called (b) on that page is the additional pair of assertions \[ \begin{aligned} (L/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^d\text{ on }L/S,\\ (P/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^g)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^g\text{ on }P/S. \end{aligned} \] Here $L/S$ and $P/S$ denote full subcategories on the corresponding structural maps. Under these additional equivalences, each fine theory is a contravariant pseudofunctor on all of $\mathcal M$. This conclusion does not require $L\cap P\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
notes: The c of ms.227 is an adjunction axiom, different from c of ms.218.

statement: The four fibration classes and Loc (7), with reference localizer. For a fundamental localizer $W$, the four classes in XVI section~4 are distinct definitions. Besides intrinsic $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, one has Grothendieck fibrations; $\operatorname{Fib}^{\mathrm{weak}}_W$, tested by all arrows $T'\to T$ over the base with $T'$ and $T$ contractible in the category-homotopy sense; and $\operatorname{Parf}_W=\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W$. Here category-homotopy contractibility means that the identity functor is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations. It implies weak contractibility of the nerve, but replacing the test family by all weakly contractible nerves is a separate assertion, not the literal definition. Let $\mathcal G_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations all of whose transport functors lie in $W$. For any arrow class $\mathcal F$, define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm A(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W,\\ \mathrm B(\mathcal F)&:\quad W_S\cap\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F/S) \subseteq W_S^u\quad\hbox{for every }S,\\ \mathrm C(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\cap W\subseteq W^u. \end{aligned} \] Loc~(7a), (7b), and (7c) are respectively $\mathrm A(\mathcal G_W)$, $\mathrm B(\mathcal G_W)$, and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G_W)$. For a reference localizer $V\subseteq W$, the conditions $\mathrm A_V,\mathrm B_V,\mathrm C_V$ replace $\mathcal G_W$ by $\mathcal G_V$. The condition $\mathrm D_V$ is $\mathrm A(\operatorname{Parf}_V)$, or its equivalent B and C forms once the hypotheses of A.17 are verified. Loc~(7F) is the factorization condition of A.11, not the inclusion of any one of these reference classes in $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
notes: Four fibration notions and eight reference/factorization variants kept separate.

statement: The implications A to B to C and replacement transfer. Let $W$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfy A.11's initial assumptions. If every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. If identities lie in $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. Suppose that each $p:X\to S$ in $\mathcal F$ admits a comparison $j_p:X\to R_p$ over $S$ in $W_S^u$, with $R_p\to S$ in $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathrm A(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. If for every map $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ between $\mathcal F$-objects the chosen comparisons extend to a commutative square $R(h)j_X=j_Yh$, then also $\mathrm B(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. Functorial replacements suffice; the proof only needs these individual commuting squares.
notes: Replacement transfer in B needs commuting squares; functoriality suffices.

statement: The full Brown implication with all its premises. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has a terminal object and pullbacks, and $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal F$ contain isomorphisms and all terminal maps, be closed under composition and pullback, and admit a factorization of every arrow as a $W$-map followed by an $\mathcal F$-map. Then \[ \mathrm A(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm B(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm C(\mathcal F). \] This is the precise abstract assertion of XVI Lemma~4.4.3. The terminal-map premise is part of the statement, not a consequence of an arbitrary intrinsic-fibration factorization.
notes: Complete relative mapping-path proof, with all terminal-map premises.

statement: The weak constant-coefficient notion does not compose. The universal weak rational cohomological fibrations of I ms.~117--118 need not be closed under composition. The failure occurs for finite categories. Consequently that notion cannot be silently substituted for the intrinsic class in A.2 or for the class in Loc~(7F).
notes: Finite covering/opfibration counterexample independently reconstructed.

statement: The local-coefficient repair has an asymmetric conclusion. Let $\mathbb D$ be a derivator in presheaf variance. Suppose that for $p:E\to B$, after every strict base change, the right direct image of every constant coefficient is locally constant and its value at each base object is canonically the right Kan extension from the strict fibre. If $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ is fully faithful on locally constant $\mathbb D$-coefficients, then the pullback $w:E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ is a constant-coefficient $\mathbb D$-equivalence. This argument does not assert full faithfulness or an equivalence on all locally constant coefficients upstairs. If the same direct-image and base-change hypothesis is required for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then the resulting cohomological-fibration class is closed under composition and pullback. The corresponding statements for left Kan extensions and homology follow by duality.
notes: Weak constant-coefficient conclusion distinguished from all local systems.

statement: Properness does not imply local constancy of fibres. The inclusion $j:\{1\}\to[1]$ is proper in Grothendieck's presheaf convention, but its comma transition over $0\to1$ is $\varnothing\to e$. Thus the assertion about proper maps at I ms.~102, companion row Ib-C003, is false already for spaces and set coefficients.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms.102; Ib-C003; GALOIS D.9; STRATA D.5
notes: Proper cosieve has comma transition empty to point.

statement: Finite products and the one-fibrant-leg pullback comparison. Assume the hypotheses of A.11 and slice replacement equivalences as in A.12. In the localized fibrant slice over $S$, the product of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ is represented by $X\times_S Y\to S$. Arbitrary derived reindexing preserves these finite products. Moreover, if $X\to S$ is intrinsic and $Y\to\overline Y\to S$ is a replacement with $Y\to\overline Y\in W$ and $\overline Y\to S$ intrinsic, then $X\times_S Y\to X\times_S\overline Y$ lies in $W$. Thus a strict pullback with one intrinsic leg computes the same relative homotopy object as replacing the other leg first. These are the formal assertions at XII ms.~241--248.
notes: Finite product universal property proved by localizing the product/diagonal adjunction.

statement: The intrinsic factorization content of the weak Quillen axioms. The conditions M2, M$'$, and M$''$ of XIII ms.~8 imply both intrinsic factorizations: every arrow factors as an intrinsic cofibration followed by a $W$-map, and as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic fibration. They consequently imply the universal-equivalence equalities of XIII Corollary~1, ms.~10, and the fibrewise assertion of XIII Proposition~4, ms.~10--11. They do not identify the designated classes $TC,TF$ with $C\cap W,F\cap W$.
notes: Historical exactness W=TF composed TC is distinguished from one-sided equality.

statement: The variance assertions of XIII section 4 are lifting adjunctions. Let $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal M)$, suppose the ordinary Kan extensions used below exist, and let the two closed lifting pairs be $(C(I),TF(I))$ and $(TC(I),F(I))$, with $C(I),TC(I)$ defined objectwise. For $u:I'\to I$ one has \[ u^*C(I)\subseteq C(I'),\quad u^*TC(I)\subseteq TC(I'), \quad u_*F(I')\subseteq F(I),\quad u_*TF(I')\subseteq TF(I), \] and \[ \begin{split} u^*F(I)\subseteq F(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!TC(I')\subseteq TC(I),\\ u^*TF(I)\subseteq TF(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!C(I')\subseteq C(I). \end{split} \] If every component of $i\backslash I'$ has an initial object and the relevant coproducts exist, then all four containments in the last two equivalences hold. In particular injective fibrant diagrams are objectwise fibrant. For a walking-arrow diagram $X_0\leftarrow X_1$, injective fibrancy is equivalent to $X_0$ fibrant and $X_1\to X_0\in F$; this also implies that $X_1$ is fibrant.
notes: Presheaf variance fixes comma orientation and walking-arrow fibrancy.

statement: Ordinary Kan extensions do not automatically descend. For $(\mathrm{Cat},W_\infty)$, ordinary limits of finite diagrams need not preserve objectwise weak equivalences. Thus an ordinary $u_*$ in XIII ms.~45--50 cannot be identified with a derived $u_*$ without a derivability or fibrancy argument.
notes: Ordinary limit of an objectwise weak equivalence may fail to be weak.

statement: The noetherian sober Alexandrov qualification adds no infinite posets. If a poset with its Alexandrov topology is noetherian and sober, the poset is finite. Hence the apparently more general admissibility qualification in XIII ms.~60--61, requiring the Alexandrov space of $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ to be noetherian and sober, introduces no genuinely infinite poset beyond the finite case.
depends_on: Alexandrov closed sets; infinite Ramsey theorem
notes: Noetherian and sober Alexandrov posets are finite; companion observation independently verified.

statement: The intrinsic finite floor does not provide all small Kan extensions. Finite limits, finite colimits, two-out-of-three, and both intrinsic factorization axioms do not imply existence of all small homotopy Kan extensions. A counterexample is the category of finite sets with isomorphisms as $W$.
depends_on: finite-set product and coproduct universal properties
notes: Finite intrinsic floor does not imply infinite Kan extensions.

statement: Closedness upgrades historical exactness to both trivial-class equalities. Let $(C,TC,F,TF)$ satisfy the weak Quillen axioms of XIII ms.~27--28, including two-out-of-three for $W$, the two factorizations, and $TC\subseteq C\cap W$, $TF\subseteq F\cap W$. If both lifting pairs are closed and $W=TF\circ TC$, then \[ TC=C\cap W,\qquad TF=F\cap W. \] Moreover $W$ is retract-closed. With the finite limits and colimits of M0 these data are a closed model structure in the original finite-limit convention. The two intrinsic containments M$''$ make this structure proper. Thus a \emph{closed exact} structure, as required by the uniform hypothesis at XIII ms.~57, is stronger than the unqualified exact structure distinguished in A.22.
notes: Closedness plus exactness DOES imply both trivial-class equalities; the added premise is essential.

statement: The uniform theorem of XIII and the exact admissibility hypothesis. Assume exactly the uniform-left hypothesis of XIII ms.~57: for every $I$ in the specified diagram domain, the objectwise classes $C(I),TC(I)$ and their right orthogonals $TF(I),F(I)$ form a closed exact weak Quillen structure for the objectwise class $W(I)$. Let $u:I'\to I$ be a functor in the domain for which the ordinary presheaf right Kan extension $u_*$ exists. Then $u_*$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrant diagrams. It consequently induces a right adjoint \[ u^*: \mathcal M(I)[W(I)^{-1}] \rightleftarrows\ \mathcal M(I')[W(I')^{-1}]:\mathbf R u_*. \] If the comma categories $I'/i$ and their inclusions into $I'$ belong to the diagram domain, the canonical pointwise formula is \[ i^*\mathbf R u_*X\ \cong\ \mathbf R\!\lim_{(I'/i)^{\mathrm{op}}}X|_{I'/i}. \] In particular every functor between finite posets is admissible under the source's hypotheses. No restriction to finite posets is necessary for admissibility once the relevant ordinary Kan extension and uniform diagram structures exist. In the historical numbering, this proves the right-hand Der~4 and Der~5 assertions of XIII ms.~61; these numbers do not mean modern Der~4 and strongness Der~5.
depends_on: A.17,A.23,A.25,A.27; Quillen 1967 I.1 Theorem 1 and I.4 Theorem 3
notes: All u with existing ordinary Kan extension are admissible under the actual uniform closed exact premise.

statement: The polarity calculation in II section 5 requires closure after a join. For any relation $R\subseteq P\times Q$, the maps $A\mapsto A^\perp=\{q\mid pRq\text{ for all }p\in A\}$ and its transpose define an antitone Galois connection on the power sets. Double orthogonality is an extensive idempotent closure; closed subsets are closed under arbitrary intersections, and their join is the closure of their union. If $P,Q$ are complete posets and the principal-polar condition (D$_0$) of II ms.~69 holds, write $c$ for the induced closure on $P$. For a subset $A\subseteq P$, its polar closure is the principal lower set \[ A^{\perp\perp}=\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee A\right) =\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee_{a\in A}c(a)\right). \] The final closure cannot be omitted from II formula~(5.20), ms.~76. One must also distinguish the element $c(\bigvee A)$ of $P$ from its principal lower set, a subset of $P$.
notes: The final closure on the supremum and the distinction element/principal lower set are required.

statement: Arbitrary unions do not preserve composition closure. The class of arrow classes containing identities and closed under both pullback and composition is not closed under arbitrary unions, contrary to the preliminary lattice description in II ms.~65--67. Intersections have that property; a join requires taking the closure of the union under the specified operations.
notes: A union of composition-closed pullback-closed classes need not compose.

statement: The bi-site remark fixes a question rather than a general theorem. At VI ms.~81--84 the data $(\mathcal M,W)$ specify the coarse slice localization, but the proposed fine classes require additional test data. The two comma tests in $\mathrm{Cat}$ have opposite variances: $X/s$ varies covariantly with $s$, and $s\backslash X$ contravariantly. In XII ms.~222 the class labelled $W^g$ uses the former tests and its universal preservation class is the smooth class discussed in Part B; XII ms.~224's $W^d$ uses the latter. The letters on an earlier page are not a substitute for this variance check. The remark that weak globular infinity-groupoids might have no useful localization theory is a suggestion at VI ms.~83--84. It is not a nonexistence theorem about fine relative theories. The attached 2026 claims about higher categories and globular groupoids remain ``claimed (OpenAI, 2026, unrefereed)'' here \citep{OpenAI2026Thomason,OpenAI2026Groupoids}; no conclusion of Part A depends on either.
notes: Higher-category 2026 claims not used as proof inputs.

statement: The literal absolute package does not imply relative Theorem A. The literal axioms Loc~(1,2,3) of XVI, with the moderate saturation of A.1, do not imply Loc~(3 bis). The failure already occurs in a triangle of finite groupoids over the one-object category $BC_2$. Thus the absolute package left undecided in POLES A.16 must be distinguished from the relative package used throughout the present paper.
notes: Component-dependent class satisfies literal moderate saturation and absolute A but fails relative A over BC2. It is not closed under all arrow retracts.

statement: The converse cocartesian assertion of XII ms.274 needs conservativity. Theorem~3$^\circ$ of XII ms.~274 is false without the conservativity premise introduced in its part~2$^\circ$. The assertion that for a map of homotopy cocartesian squares $f_0,f_3\in W$ imply $f_1,f_2\in W$ fails even when $W$ is strongly saturated and the intrinsic cofibration factorization exists. Corollary~1 on that page is also false without that extra premise.
notes: Strongly saturated isomorphisms on finite sets refute the converse and the unqualified corollary.

statement: Stabilizers alone do not define the antitone correspondence of the cancelled section. For arbitrary arrow classes $A$, the operation $A\mapsto\operatorname{Stab}(A)$ is not antitone. Thus the first, cancelled proposal in II section~4 cannot be used in place of the corrected transporter construction in section~6.
notes: Stabilizers are not antitone for arbitrary input classes.
